title: {{NAME}} and the Robot Who Learned to Purr
moral: The best inventions are made to help others feel less alone.
character_anchor: Bright children's book cartoon illustration, bold outlines, vivid flat colours. {{NAME}}, a young boy with brown hair and blue eyes, wearing a silver-grey hoodie with a pawprint patch, dark jeans, and white high-tops — same child, same face, same exact outfit in every image.

pages.content:
{{NAME}} built the robot for the animals at the rescue shelter down the road.

The shelter had more animals than volunteers, and the night shift was lonely for the cats and dogs and one elderly rabbit named Geoffrey who had been there two years and didn't like the dark.

The robot was small enough to walk the cages without getting in the way, with a heat-sensor chest panel that glowed warm orange and a speaker that played a heartbeat.

{{NAME}} called it PATCH.

pages.content:
The first night, PATCH trundled into the shelter and stopped in front of Geoffrey's hutch.

The old rabbit pressed his nose to the wire and sniffed. PATCH's chest light pulsed slowly, like breathing.

Geoffrey settled down onto his paws. His nose kept twitching, but the rigid tense line of his back slowly softened.

{{NAME}} watched through the window and felt something warm spread through his chest that had nothing to do with his hoodie.

pages.content:
By the third night, PATCH had developed its own method.

For the dogs: a slow back-and-forth rolling that mimicked being patted.

For the kittens: a high-frequency vibration of its chassis that was a very convincing purr.

For Geoffrey: just the steady heartbeat and warm light.

{{NAME}} hadn't programmed any of this. PATCH had figured it out by watching what each animal responded to.

"You're learning," {{NAME}} said, amazed.

PATCH beeped twice. {{NAME}} was starting to understand that meant yes.

pages.content:
The shelter manager called {{NAME}}'s parents to say that since PATCH arrived, adoptions had gone up forty percent.

Animals that seemed too anxious for families were calmer. Geoffrey had stopped hiding. Two dogs who had stopped eating were eating again.

{{NAME}} sat in the shelter that afternoon and watched PATCH navigate the room: patient, unhurried, stopping exactly where it was needed.

He thought: this is what good looks like.

pages.content:
That night, {{NAME}} went to say goodnight to PATCH before heading home.

PATCH was in the corner with Geoffrey. The robot's chest light pulsed at the pace of a sleeping heartbeat. Geoffrey was pressed against its side, eyes closed, utterly peaceful.

{{NAME}} crouched down and put his hand on PATCH's smooth shell. Warmth hummed back through his palm.

He walked home through the quiet street, looking up at the stars.

Somewhere behind him, through the shelter walls, he could just hear it: a small, steady, mechanical purr.
